title: Complete Entanglement Structure of the Kitaev Honeycomb Spin Liquid from Exact Tensor Networks
abstract: While most of the features of the Kitaev honeycomb model are already clarified from the combined ${\mathbb Z}_2$ plaquette and Majorana fermion picture, we show that retrieving the exact quantum many-body form gives a clue to fix the remaining issues on its spin liquid property. We provide an exact two-dimensional tensor network description of a full set of solutions from a random product state, by sequential quantum-number projection and Gutzwiller projection, both expressed as local matrix-product operators of dimension $D=2$. The ground and excited states share the same bond dimension yet exhibit distinct Schmidt spectra, distinguishing their area-law and volume-law entanglement. We demonstrate that the topological entanglement entropy emerges {\it for all eigenstates only after} the Gutzwiller projection onto the physical spin Hilbert space, where the gauge constraint removes exactly half of the Schmidt states. This establishes that excited states are likewise topologically ordered. We further show that there exists a projection-induced collapse of the wave function into a single gauge sector in the Parton mean-field states that is known to give a good description of the spin liquids. The demonstrations on the $S=1/2$ kagome and triangular Heisenberg models suggest that the present perspective is applied to a wider class of models hosting ${\mathbb Z}_2$ spin liquids. Our finding visualizes a bulk-boundary correspondence with the Wilson-loop characterization of topological order.
summary: This work develops an exact Tensor Network framework to characterize the entanglement structure of the Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid. By systematically applying local projectors and the Gutzwiller projection, the authors demonstrate that topological order is robustly encoded in the entanglement spectrum, even in excited states. This provides a powerful, mathematically rigorous method for studying Z2 spin liquids in strongly correlated materials.
main_problem: To provide an exact quantum many-body description of the Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid (QSL) wavefunction, specifically addressing the difficulty of treating the full quantum state after Gutzwiller projection.
main_result: The authors establish that the topological entanglement entropy emerges only after the Gutzwiller projection, confirming that excited states in the Kitaev model are also topologically ordered.
method: The study employs an exact two-dimensional Tensor Network (TN) description, constructing the eigenstate by sequentially applying local projectors derived from the Majorana Hamiltonian, followed by the Gutzwiller projection.
model_or_system: The primary system is the Kitaev honeycomb model, a canonical platform for a Z2 spin liquid. The Hamiltonian is analyzed using both its original spin form and its equivalent quadratic Majorana fermion form.
key_observables: Topological Entanglement Entropy (EE), Schmidt spectra, and the presence of conserved Z2 quantum numbers.
important_parameters: The bond dimension used in the TN representation is kept small ($D=2$), and the analysis compares U(1) vs Z2 symmetry breaking.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that the exact TN representation can be constructed via sequential projection steps, and the analysis relies on the validity of the Gutzwiller projection formalism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the TN construction involving MPS and MPOs for projectors, the braiding process, and comparisons of entanglement entropy ($S_\alpha$) and Schmidt values ($\lambda_\ell$) between U(1) and Z2 symmetry regimes for kagome and triangular lattices.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the model and the challenge of the full quantum state. It then details the TN construction using successive projections (Majorana and Gutzwiller) to obtain the exact eigenstate. Finally, it analyzes the resulting entanglement structure and its dependence on symmetry breaking.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of TNs to extract exact entanglement properties, especially the emergence of topological order only after the Gutzwiller projection, provides a powerful, non-variational tool for understanding strongly correlated quantum phases.
